artifacts.summary: 5-phase plan: independently re-execute the per-site empirical grep word-boundary audit (ugrep-exposed Markdown sites and .sh/hook sites), then author, index, and deploy the portability guidance note.

memory_candidates.content: In this environment `grep` resolves to two different engines depending on invocation context, and the difference is load-bearing for any regex-portability audit. A command typed or pasted directly into an agent's Bash-tool shell hits a non-exported shell function that exec's ugrep (7.8.4), whose POSIX/DFA `-E` engine mis-evaluates `\b` COMPOSITIONALLY: a `\b` appearing downstream of an earlier `\b`-anchored subexpression separated by a wildcard run (e.g. `[^|]*`) can fail even though every fragment matches in isolation and `-P` on the identical pattern matches. A pattern inside a `.sh` script or hook executed as a subprocess (`bash file.sh`, hook runner) resolves instead to GNU grep 3.12, which is immune. Consequence: before auditing or repairing any `\b` pattern, determine which context runs it (`type grep` at top level; `bash -c 'grep --version'` for the subprocess case) -- and never generalize one site's result to another, since only a CHAIN of two or more `\b`-anchored subexpressions is at risk, while a lone `\b` or single `\b...\b` bracket works under both engines.
